messages:
ana: heads up — since ~17:12 UTC we're seeing nvme metadata flips on /dev/nvme0n1 (scratch) in a subset of us-west1 hosts. GPU attach failures and nodes quarantined. Currently 12 hosts affected, ~20 pending GPU requests blocked. investigating :eyes:

mike: any obvious error in dmesg?

ana: pasted a log snippet from one host:
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme0: error: metadata checksum mismatch: blockmap cksum=0x1a2b, expected=0x3c4d
[ 1234.568012] scrubber: writeback failed: -5 (EIO)
[ 1234.568999] scratch-mount: failing mount, refusing attach
```

sara: is this after the nightly scrub rollout? we had a scrub cadence change last night.

jordan: yup scrub job rolled at ~04:00. scrub logs show aborted flushes on these exact hosts. looks like scrub + janitor overlap created partial metadata writes. not full corruption but checksum flips.

kyle: this is ephemeral data right? safe to remount read-only or run repair? what's risk to running fsck/repair while attached?

ana: ephemeral only (KV cache). risk is lost cache only. plan I'm proposing:
  1) scale down allocator for us-west1 GPU pool to stop new attaches
  2) drain the 12 affected hosts (mark unsched)
  3) run scrub/repair with --force and `blkdiscard`/reformat on scratch devices, rolling 4 hosts at a time to avoid region-wide capacity hit
  4) bring hosts back into pool and monitor attach success

ops-bot: maintenance ticket MN-4521 created for us-west1 nvme metadata repairs. ETA window 3–6h.

mike: note on cost: 20 pending GPUs will overflow into other regions or trigger extra reserved allocations -> estimate $1.2k/hr if we spill. batching will minimize this.

jordan: agree. suggest 4-concurrent repairs to balance time vs cost. also file a patch for the janitor/scrub scheduling to avoid overlap (postmortem item).

sara: please check SMART temps and reassign any drives with rising temp or reallocated sector counts before rejoin. if SMART bad, send replacement flow.

kyle: I'll open hardware tickets for NVMe IDs: nvme-wwn-0xabc123... and put them on hold if SMART > threshold.

ana: starting drains now. will post per-host status. tagging @kyle for hw. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks. ping when first 4 are back so we can confirm attach rate and throttling behavior.

jordan: quick command I'm running to repro/validate after repair:
```bash
# run on repaired host
sudo systemctl stop ephemeral-cleaner.service
blkdiscard /dev/nvme0n1 && mkfs.ext4 -L scratch /dev/nvme0n1
mount /dev/nvme0n1 /scratch && systemctl start ephemeral-cleaner.service
# then run gpu-attach smoke: ./tools/gpu_attach_smoke.sh --region us-west1 --count 5
```

sara: perfect. please also collect `nvme-cli` smart log and scrubber traces for the postmortem.

ops-bot: update: MN-4521 status -> in_progress (ana). assigned to eng-infra.

ana: update 17:45 UTC — drained first 4 hosts, started forced scrub+reformat. two hosts had SMART reallocated sector > 5 — flagged for replacement and not rejoined. others proceeding.

mike: good. keep an eye on spot scaling in other regions. I'll raise temporary quota if needed.

ana: will post final once all batches done. current target to finish rolling repairs in ~4 hours.

kyle: hw tickets opened: HT-9982, HT-9983 for two failed nvmes.

jordan: adding cleanup scheduling guard to janitor: PR in progress, will link once ready.

sara: thanks team. :coffee:

ana: final note — no user data at risk; main impact is provisioning latency. we'll include mitigation steps in the incident doc.
